We’re hiring! The Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC) of UNESCO is currently seeking talented professionals to become part of its global team advancing ocean knowledge, warning systems, capacity development and data exchange worldwide. Chief of Secion - Tsunami Resilience Take a leadership role in advancing global tsunami preparedness and early warning systems. As Chief of Section, you will guide IOC's Tsunami Programme, coordinate regional warning and mitigation systems, strengthen capacity development initiatives, engage international partners, and support Member States in building resilience against tsunamis and other coastal hazards. Deadline: 7 September 2026, Midnight Paris Time Apply: https://lnkd.in/enTmKffy Programme Specialist - Capacity Development & Ocean Literacy Lead IOC's global efforts to strengthen ocean capacity development and ocean literacy across Member States. This role focuses on designing and managing international programmes, fostering partnerships, supporting the OceanTeacher Global Academy (OTGA), and helping communities, institutions and stakeholders build the knowledge and skills needed to understand, protect and sustainably manage the ocean. Deadline: 31 August 2026, Midnight Paris Time Apply: https://lnkd.in/eghG9Zch Programme Specialist - Global Ocean Observing System Help drive the world's leading ocean observation network. This position provides strategic and operational leadership for the Global Ocean Observing System (GOOS), working with governments, scientific institutions and international partners to strengthen ocean observations, support climate and ocean health applications, promote FAIR data sharing, and enhance global understanding of our changing ocean. Deadline: 7 September 2026, Midnight Paris Time Apply: https://lnkd.in/eTWecDHN Programme Specialist - IOC Data and Information Exchange (IODE) Lead IOC's efforts to advance global ocean data and information exchange. The successful candidate will oversee the development of data standards, interoperability and exchange systems, strengthen the capacity of Member States to manage ocean data, coordinate international partnerships, and ensure that ocean information remains accessible, reliable and impactful for science and society.
